# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination — Request for Reconsideration

**Jordan Kimura**
[Street address]
[City, State ZIP]
[Phone number]
[Email address]

**Date:** [Date I am mailing this letter]

**To:** MedStar Family Choice — Member Appeals
[Use the appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**RE:** Appeal of denial dated August 25, 2026
**Member:** Jordan Kimura
**Member ID:** W450262274
**Reference number:** POC-9297E0E467-45895
**Service denied:** Bunion surgery (hallux valgus), CPT 28296
**Plan:** MedStar Family Choice (Commercial/ACA), Maryland

---

## A note on the policy and criteria

I was not given a copy of the medical policy or the clinical review criteria that were used to deny my surgery, so I am not able to quote the plan's own standards back to you in this letter. Nothing in this letter is presented as the plan's language. The denial notice states only that my request was reviewed under the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria, without identifying them or stating what imaging findings would satisfy them. I am therefore appealing based on the facts in my medical record, and I am asking below that the plan send me the criteria it actually applied.

## What I am asking for

I am appealing the denial of coverage for the bunion surgery (CPT 28296) that my surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, MD, orthopedic surgery, requested for me. The denial notice, dated August 25, 2026, gives one reason: that the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure. I am asking MedStar Family Choice to reconsider that decision and to approve the procedure. My surgeon has documented that this surgery is needed, and the records submitted with the prior authorization include the imaging, the exam findings, and the months of treatment I tried first.

## Request for the criteria that were applied

I am requesting, in writing and free of charge, the specific rule or criterion that was relied on to deny my claim. I understand my plan uses InterQual, which is licensed software rather than a publicly posted document, and that federal ERISA and ACA appeal rules entitle me to the specific criterion used in my case regardless. Please send me **the InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text applied to my determination**, along with any internal medical policy used in this review. The plan holds these documents; I do not. Without them, I cannot see what imaging measurement or finding the reviewer expected, and I cannot fully respond to the reason given for the denial. If the plan has a specific imaging threshold, I am asking the plan to state it in writing along with the reconsideration decision.

## What my records show

These are the facts as they appear in the prior authorization packet that was submitted on my behalf:

**Imaging.** Weight-bearing foot radiographs taken on July 26, 2026 measured a hallux valgus angle of 38 degrees and an intermetatarsal angle of 17 degrees. These are objective, measured findings from weight-bearing films — the imaging the denial says does not support the surgery is imaging that documents deformity at both of these angles.

**Symptoms and duration.** I have had 18 months of progressive pain in the foot, and it is not relieved by rest.

**Non-surgical treatment I completed first.** I tried activity modification, wide toe-box footwear, and a custom orthotic over 8 weeks, from May 19, 2026 to July 14, 2026, completing 20 visits. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note. I also took NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief, and I had a corticosteroid injection on May 7, 2026, which gave me only 4 weeks of partial relief.

**Exam findings.** My exam documented positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain.

**Function and risk.** I cannot tolerate closed shoes, and my record documents ulceration risk over the prominence.

**Surgical risk factors.** My records note no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker.

Taken together, my file documents measured radiographic deformity, a positive exam, 18 months of progressive symptoms, and a full course of conservative care — footwear changes, a custom orthotic, months of NSAIDs, and an injection — that did not give me lasting relief. I am not able to point to the sentence in the plan's criteria that this evidence satisfies, because I have not been given that sentence. If the plan believes a specific imaging finding is missing, I am asking the plan to identify it so that my surgeon can respond to it directly.

## Closing request

I respectfully ask MedStar Family Choice to overturn the denial of CPT 28296 and approve the surgery my surgeon has documented that I need. In the alternative, I ask that the plan provide the InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text applied to my determination, so that this appeal can be decided against a standard I am able to see.

I understand my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, by **February 21, 2027**, and I am submitting it within that period. I am sending this to the appeal address printed on my denial letter; if there is a different address or process for member appeals, please tell me and I will resubmit promptly. (Members can also call the number on the back of the insurance card to ask where member appeals are filed.)

Please send your decision, and the criteria requested above, to me in writing at the address at the top of this letter. I am glad to provide any additional records you need, and my surgeon's office can be reached at [surgeon's office phone number].

Thank you for taking another look at this.

Sincerely,

**[Signature]**

Jordan Kimura
Member ID: W450262274
Date of birth: [Date of birth]
Reference number: POC-9297E0E467-45895

**Enclosures:** [List what you are attaching — e.g., copy of the denial notice dated 2026-08-25; weight-bearing radiograph report dated 2026-07-26; physical therapy discharge note; surgeon's office notes and letter of medical necessity]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
